title: Amitabh Bachchan Greets Fans From Behind Bulletproof Shield After Bomb Threat
excerpt: The Sunday darshan at Jalsa went ahead under tight security, with Abhishek Bachchan beside his father, weeks after a threat email naming the bungalow reached Mumbai Police.
body:
• Amitabh Bachchan kept his Sunday tradition of greeting fans outside his Mumbai home, Jalsa, this week — but waved from behind a transparent protective shell installed on his raised platform.
  • His son Abhishek Bachchan stood beside him as security personnel monitored the crowd gathered outside the Juhu bungalow.
  • Mumbai Police received information on October 23 about a bomb-threat email, sent to a school in Bandra-Kurla Complex, that named Jalsa and the dates October 31 and November 27, according to IANS reporting.
  • The same letter reportedly named singer-actor Diljit Dosanjh in connection with a purported attack at Mahalaxmi Racecourse on November 27; police have launched an investigation and have not confirmed the reason for the new enclosure.

For decades, Sunday evenings outside Jalsa, Amitabh Bachchan's home in Juhu, Mumbai, have followed the same script: hundreds of fans gather at the gate, and the actor steps onto a small raised platform to wave. This Sunday, November 1, the ritual held — but the platform had changed. Bachchan greeted the crowd standing inside a transparent protective shell, described in IANS visuals as a bulletproof enclosure, with his son Abhishek Bachchan beside him and several security personnel posted around them.

The threat behind the security step-up

The added protection follows reports of a bomb-threat email. According to IANS, Mumbai Police received information about the email on October 23. It was reportedly sent to a school in the Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) area, and police launched an investigation.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ZwoppgpAx6s

The letter referred to Jalsa and mentioned October 31 and November 27 as dates for alleged attacks. It also named singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh in connection with a purported bomb attack at Mumbai's Mahalaxmi Racecourse on November 27, though the threat was not directed at Dosanjh explicitly. The letter included pro-Khalistan slogans, and the threats were attributed to a group calling itself the "Khalistan National Army," IANS reported. The exact reason for installing the enclosure has not been officially confirmed.

The ritual goes on

What did not change was the appearance itself. Bachchan waved to admirers as he does every Sunday, and Abhishek stayed close by, watching the crowd while his father greeted fans, Cinema Express reported. The Sunday darshan, as fans call it, has been a fixture of Mumbai celebrity culture for years, drawing crowds to the bungalow's gates every week.

The appearance also comes as Bachchan manages his workload on medical advice. He recently told followers on his Tumblr blog that doctors had advised him to take more rest as part of his recovery, and that he would be less active on social media for a time.

"Yet more rest needed .. adjusting .. thinking and wondering .. the human body and its uniqueness."

— Amitabh Bachchan, on his blog

On screen, he remains busy: he is currently hosting the quiz show Kaun Banega Crorepati. For the diaspora audience that grew up on his films, the image from Sunday — the wave unchanged, the setting fortified — captures both the durability of the ritual and the seriousness with which Mumbai Police are treating the threat.
nri_angle: For diaspora fans who grew up on Bachchan's films, the fortified Sunday darshan at Jalsa shows a beloved ritual continuing under an active police investigation.
